$comment: Entries store the SHA-256 of the matched value, never the value itself.
NEVER allowlist a real credential. A SHA-256 of a low-entropy value is
brute-forceable, so an entry here confirms a guess. Rotate instead.
Only PLACEHOLDER, SYNTHETIC_TEST_FIXTURE and PUBLIC_UPSTREAM_MATERIAL belong here.
Every entry MUST cite the audit section that justifies the classification.
Adding an entry is a publication decision: it is reviewed like a code change.

accepted.reason: Literal string 'password' in the sample DATABASE_URL. Never a live credential.
Base64 of 'testsecretforunittests' used by the Svix HMAC unit tests. Not issued by Clerk or Stripe.

YouTube InnerTube ANDROID client key shipped in the public YouTube Android application and hardcoded by every major transcript library. Not a StriveX credential; overridable via YOUTUBE_INNERTUBE_API_KEY.

The string 'openbooklm' used as a Postgres password in three places, none of them a credential: the public sample config, where it is a development default for running against your own Postgres and where the Compose stack publishes no database port at all, and the two workflows, where it belongs to a throwaway pgvector service container set in plain text in the same file. Introduced by EP-004, after the original audit ran.

Credential-shaped probe in `production_looking_values_are_rejected`, the test that proves the corpus validator refuses production-looking identifiers. Proving a detector fires requires a value the detector matches, so this scan necessarily matches it too. The value is `sk-` followed by the Latin alphabet and 012345; no issuer produces that.
